trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Sentences under 25 words. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: Quantitative Analyst - Counterparty Credit Risk DCEM
Company: Absa Group
About the company: Empowering Africa’s tomorrow, together…one story at a time. With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise.
Purpose of the role: Provide independent analysis and oversight of counterparty credit exposure across derivative portfolios, with a focus on Potential Future Exposure (PFE), mark-to-market (MTM), margin and limit utilization. Partner with Front Office, Credit Risk, Quantitative Risk, Finance and Technology teams to support pre-deal assessments, complex transaction analysis and informed credit decisions. Maintain a strong control environment by monitoring data quality, investigating exposure exceptions and ensuring that risk information is accurate, complete and appropriately escalated. Support the development, testing, validation and ongoing enhancement of counterparty credit risk models, systems and reporting processes, including Sigma, QlikView and associated ETL layers. Deliver clear portfolio analytics, stress testing and regulatory or management reporting, while translating technical counterparty credit risk concepts for senior stakeholders and governance forums.
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - Calculate, analyse and explain PFE, MTM and related exposure measures for OTC derivatives, Securities Financing Transactions (SFTs), and structured products.
  - Support Front Office and Credit Risk stakeholders with pre-deal calculations, ad hoc exposure analysis, limit setting and limit-utilisation queries.
  - Assess the drivers of counterparty exposure at trade, netting-set and portfolio level, including the impact of collateral, margining, legal agreements and credit risk mitigation.
  - Provide analysis and interpretation of complex transactions to support credit assessments and risk decisions.
  - Monitor exposure and limit exceptions, investigate material movements and ensure timely escalation and resolution.
  - Develop a sound working knowledge of PFE methodologies, model assumptions and the end-to-end exposure reporting process.
  - Collaborate with quantitative and risk teams on model calibration, validation, back-testing and annual model reviews.
  - Perform sensitivity analysis, stress testing and scenario analysis to assess the effect of market shocks and adverse conditions on counterparty exposure.
  - Produce detailed portfolio analytics, including concentration, sector, wrong-way risk and other relevant counterparty risk views.
  - Support stakeholder training and provide clear explanations of exposure methodologies, results and limitations.
  - Monitor the accuracy and completeness of exposure data through effective data-quality controls, reconciliations, reporting and escalation.
  - Assist with user acceptance testing for Sigma releases, model enhancements and other system changes.
  - Provide clear business requirements to Technology teams and support testing, implementation and issue resolution.
  - Help maintain and improve the existing risk system framework, including Sigma, QlikView models and relevant ETL processes.
  - Identify opportunities to automate and streamline reporting, manual overrides, marginal risking and other recurring processes, while supporting strategic solutions.
  - Document processes, methodologies, controls, test results and model changes to an appropriate audit and governance standard.
  - Prepare accurate and timely regular and ad hoc counterparty credit risk reports for management, governance forums and regulatory authorities.
  - Support daily margin reporting to the Prudential Authority and monthly stress-testing, scenario-analysis, KRI and management-information reporting.
  - Prepare concise presentations and commentary that explain key exposure movements, concentrations, emerging risks and control matters.
  - Represent the team in counterparty credit risk workstreams and contribute PFE and MTM considerations to cross-functional discussions.
  - Maintain awareness of relevant market developments, regulatory changes and industry practice, including SA-CCR and margin requirements.
Must-have requirements:
  - Bachelor's Degree or Advanced Diploma in Risk Management, Financial Risk Management, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics or a related quantitative discipline.
  - One to three years of relevant experience in counterparty credit risk, derivatives or quantitative risk.
  - Working knowledge of financial markets, derivative products, exposure measurement and risk metrics.
  - Understanding of counterparty credit risk concepts, including netting, collateral, legal agreements, margining and credit risk mitigation.
  - Ability to interpret complex datasets, perform root-cause analysis and translate results into practical risk insights.
  - Advanced Excel capability.
  - Knowledge of model governance, validation, back-testing, stress testing and data-quality control principles.
  - Bachelor`s Degrees and Advanced Diplomas: Business, Commerce and Management Studies (Required)
Nice-to-have:
  - Professional qualifications such as FRM or CA(SA) are advantageous.
  - Exposure to counterparty credit risk regulation, including SA-CCR and margin requirements, is advantageous.
  - Experience with Power BI, Python, SQL or other automation and analytics tools is advantageous.
  - Experience with risk systems, data visualisation tools and data-processing workflows; Sigma and QlikView exposure is advantageous.
Location: Sandton
Team notes: Front Office and Trading Desks; Credit Risk and Counterparty Credit Risk teams; Quantitative Risk and Model Validation; Technology, Data and Infrastructure teams; Regulatory Reporting, senior management and governance forums
Employment equity statement: Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.
Accessibility statement: We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.

Quantitative Analyst - Counterparty Credit Risk

Absa Group

Sandton

About us
Empowering Africa's tomorrow, together…one story at a time. With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise.

About the role
You will provide independent analysis and oversight of counterparty credit exposure across derivative portfolios, focusing on Potential Future Exposure (PFE), mark-to-market (MTM), margin and limit utilisation. You will support pre-deal assessments and credit decisions, keep exposure data accurate and complete, and help develop and test the models, systems and reporting that the bank relies on.

Your team
You will work with Front Office and trading desks, Credit Risk and Counterparty Credit Risk teams, Quantitative Risk and Model Validation, Technology, Data and Infrastructure teams, and Regulatory Reporting, senior management and governance forums.

What you'll do
• Calculate, analyse and explain PFE, MTM and related exposure measures for OTC derivatives, Securities Financing Transactions and structured products.
• Support Front Office and Credit Risk stakeholders with pre-deal calculations, ad hoc exposure analysis, limit setting and limit-utilisation queries.
• Assess the drivers of exposure at trade, netting-set and portfolio level, including collateral, margining, legal agreements and credit risk mitigation.
• Interpret complex transactions to support credit assessments and risk decisions.
• Monitor exposure and limit exceptions, investigate material movements and escalate and resolve them on time.
• Perform sensitivity analysis, stress testing and scenario analysis to measure the effect of market shocks on counterparty exposure.
• Produce portfolio analytics covering concentration, sector, wrong-way risk and other counterparty risk views.
• Monitor the accuracy and completeness of exposure data through data-quality controls, reconciliations, reporting and escalation.
• Work with quantitative and risk teams on model calibration, validation, back-testing and annual model reviews.
• Assist with user acceptance testing for Sigma releases, model enhancements and other system changes, and give Technology teams clear business requirements.
• Help maintain and improve Sigma, QlikView models and relevant ETL processes, and automate recurring reporting, manual overrides and marginal risking.
• Prepare regular and ad hoc reports for management, governance forums and regulatory authorities, including daily margin reporting to the Prudential Authority and monthly stress-testing, scenario-analysis, KRI and management-information reporting.
• Write concise presentations and commentary explaining exposure movements, concentrations, emerging risks and control matters.
• Document processes, methodologies, controls, test results and model changes to an audit and governance standard.
• Support stakeholder training by explaining exposure methodologies, results and limitations.

What you need
• Bachelor's Degree or Advanced Diploma in Risk Management, Financial Risk Management, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics or a related quantitative discipline (Business, Commerce and Management Studies required).
• One to three years of relevant experience in counterparty credit risk, derivatives or quantitative risk.
• Working knowledge of financial markets, derivative products, exposure measurement and risk metrics.
• Understanding of counterparty credit risk concepts, including netting, collateral, legal agreements, margining and credit risk mitigation.
• Ability to interpret complex datasets, perform root-cause analysis and translate results into practical risk insights.
• Advanced Excel capability, plus knowledge of model governance, validation, back-testing, stress testing and data-quality control principles.

Nice to have
• Professional qualifications such as FRM or CA(SA).
• Exposure to counterparty credit risk regulation, including SA-CCR and margin requirements.
• Experience with Power BI, Python, SQL or other automation and analytics tools.
• Experience with risk systems, data visualisation tools and data-processing workflows, including Sigma and QlikView.

We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.

Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.

You will also represent the team in counterparty credit risk workstreams and keep track of market developments, regulatory changes and industry practice, including SA-CCR and margin requirements.
